label: LovKG
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{LovKG}
    Let $n \geq 2r$. Then
    $$
        \chi(G(n,r,0)) = n-2r+2.
    $$
head: environment

label: trivial
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{trivial}
$$
\chi(G)\le\chi_L(G)\le\Delta(G)+1,
$$
where $\Delta(G)$ denotes the maximum degree of $G$.
head: environment

label: Zakharov
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Zakharov}
    For fixed integers $r > s \geq 0$ we have
    $$
    \chi_L(G(n,r,s))=O(n^{s+1}\ln n).
    $$
head: environment

label: Low1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Low1}
    For every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and any $2 \leq r \leq n^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ we have
    $$
        \chi_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq C_{\varepsilon}n\ln n
    $$
    for some $C_\varepsilon > 0$.
head: environment

label: Up
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Up}
    For any $r$ and $n$ such that $2r \leq n$ we have
    $$
        \chi_L(G(n,r,0))\le n\ln\frac{n}{r}+n.
    $$
head: environment

label: Low2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Low2}
    Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $3 \leq r \leq \sqrt\frac{n}{1+\varepsilon}$. Then
    $$
    \chi_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \left(\frac{r-2}{8r}-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)n\ln n
    $$
    for all $n > n_0(\varepsilon)$.
head: environment

label: main_gnrs
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main_gnrs}
    Fix integers $s > 0$ and $r \geq 2s+3$. Then
    $$
        \chi_L(G(n,r,s)) \geq (1-o(1))\frac{r-2s-1}{8\ln 2\, \binom{r}{s+1}}\binom{n}{s+1}\ln n.
    $$
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a set of all possible distributions on the collection of independent sets in graph $G$. Define 
    $$
        \chi_f(G) := \min_{\mathbf{Q} \in \mathcal{Q}} \max_{v \in G} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I),
    $$
    where $I$ is a random independent set. We call $\chi_f(G)$ the fractional chromatic number of $G$.
head: environment

label: UB1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{UB1}
    For any graph $G$ on $n$ vertices we have 
    $$
        \chi_L(G) \leq k = \lceil\chi_f(G)(\ln n + 1)\rceil.
    $$
head: environment

label: UB2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{UB2}
    Let $G$ be a graph on $n \geq 2$ vertices. Let $a(G) = n\chi^{-1}_f(G)$ (note that $a(G) = \alpha(G)$ for vertex transitive graphs). Assume that $\frac{\chi_f(G)}{\sqrt{\ln a(G)}} > 10\ln n$ and $a(G) \geq 3$. Then
    $$
        \chi_L(G) \leq k = \lceil\chi_f(G)\left(\ln a(G) + \ln \ln a(G)\right)\rceil + 3\left\lceil\frac{\chi_f(G)}{\sqrt{\ln a(G)}}\right\rceil
    $$
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Fix $r$ and $s$ such that $r > 2s+1$ and $s \geq 0$. We have 
    $$
        \chi_L(G(n,r,s)) \leq (1+o(1))\frac{r-s-1}{\binom{r}{s+1}}\binom{n}{s+1}\ln n.
    $$
head: environment

label: main_kgnr
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main_kgnr}
	Let $n \geq 1000$, $r \geq 4\ln n$, $20r \leq n$. Then
	$$
		\chi_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \frac{n}{120}\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right).
	$$

label: SuperSat
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{SuperSat}
    Fix two integers, $r$ and $s$, $s > 0$ and $r > 2s + 2$. For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta = \delta(\varepsilon, r, s) > 0$ such that for all $n \geq n_0(\varepsilon,r,s)$ and any $A \subset G$ such that $|A| > (1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}$ we have $e(A) > \frac{\delta |A|^2}{n^s}$.
head: environment

label: Spectr
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Spectr}
	Fix $r$, $n$ such that $2r \leq n$. Let $A$ be the set of vertices of $G(n,r,0)$ such that $|A| > \alpha(G(n,r,0)) = \binom{n-1}{r-1}$. Then
	$$
		e(A) \geq \frac{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}{2\binom{n-1}{r-1}}|A|\left(|A| - \binom{n-1}{r-1}\right).
	$$
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Consider a graph $G$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a collection of subsets of its vertices satisfying the following properties.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Each independent subset of $G$ is contained in at least one of the sets $C \in \mathcal{C}$.

        \item For each set $C \in \mathcal{C}$ its size does not exceed $K\alpha(G)$.

        \item The cardinality $|\mathcal{C}|$ does not exceed $f$.
    \end{enumerate}
    We call such a collection $(K, f)$-container.
head: environment

label: mainL
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{mainL}
    Fix $s > 0$, $r \geq 2s+2$ and $\varepsilon > 0$. There exists $\delta = \delta_{\varepsilon, r, s} > 0$ such that there exists a $(1 + \varepsilon, \exp\left(\delta n^s \ln^2 n\right))$-container in $G(n,r,s)$.
head: environment

label: mainLKG
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{mainLKG}
    	Fix $r$, $n$ such that $r \geq 10$, $n \geq 1000$, $3r \leq n$ and take any $1 \geq \varepsilon > \frac{1}{n}$. Then there exists a $\left(1 + \varepsilon,2\left(\frac{e\binom{n}{r}}{k}\right)^k\right)$-container in $G(n,r,0)$, where 
	$$
		k =  \left\lfloor\frac{2(2+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\varepsilon\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}\right\rfloor.
	$$

    For instance, there exists a $\left(2, 2\left(\frac{e\binom{n}{r}}{k}\right)^k\right)$-container in $G(n,r,0)$, where 
	$$
		k =  \left\lfloor\frac{6\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}\right\rfloor.
	$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that $G(n,r,0)$ is an $(N, d, \lambda)$ graph with $N = \binom{n}{r}$, $d = \binom{n-r}{r}$ and $\lambda = \binom{n-r-1}{r-1}$. Note that $d = \frac{n-r}{r}\lambda$, $N = \frac{n}{r}\alpha$.

	We thus have
	$$
		2e(A) \geq \frac{d}{N}|A|^2 - \frac{\lambda}{N}|A|(N-|A|) = \frac{d+\lambda}{N}|A|^2 - \lambda|A| = \frac{\lambda}{\alpha}\left(\frac{\frac{n-r}{r}+1}{\frac{n}{r}}|A|^2-|A|\alpha\right) = \frac{\lambda}{\alpha}|A|(|A| - \alpha),
	$$
	which is exactly what we need.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us consider an arbitrary independent set $I$ in $G(n,r,s)$ and perform the following algorithm. Put $V_0 = V_{G(n,r,s)}$ and $U_0 = \varnothing$. At $i$-th step select the vertex $v_i$ with maximum degree in $G(n,r,s)[V_{i-1}]$. If $v_i \in I$, put $V_i = V_{i-1} \setminus (\{v_i\} \cup N(v_i))$ and $U_i = U_{i-1} \cup \{v_i\}$. If $v_i \notin I$, we put $V_i = V_{i-1} \setminus \{v_i\}$ and $U_i = U_{i-1}$. We stop whenever $|V_i| \leq (1+\varepsilon/2)\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}$. In the remaining part of the proof index $i$ denotes the last step of the algorithm (that is, $|V_i| \leq (1+\varepsilon/2)\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}$).

    Let us obtain some properties of $V_i$ and $U_i$. First of all, let us notice that $V_i$ is a function of $U_i$. Indeed, if two independent sets $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the same on $V_{G(n,r,s)} \setminus V_i$, the algorithm does just the same steps for them and thus the final sets will be the same. This means that the number of different $V_i \cup U_i$ over all $I$ is exactly the same as the number of different $U_i$. 

    The second thing to notice is that whenever we add a vertex to $U_{j+1}$, we throw out $\Delta(G(n,r,s)[V_j])+1$ vertices from $V_j$. This can be trivially bounded from below with the use of Theorem \ref{SuperSat}: 

    $$
        \Delta(G(n,r,s)[V_j]) \geq \frac{2e(G(n,r,s)[V_j])}{|V_j|} \geq \frac{2\delta|V_j|}{n^s}.
    $$

    We thus have 
    $$
    |V_{j+1}| \leq \left(1-\frac{C}{n^s}\right)|V_j| \Rightarrow 1 \leq |V_{i-1}| \leq \left(1-\frac{C}{n^s}\right)^{|U_i|-1}\binom{n}{r} \Rightarrow |U_i| \leq \Tilde{C}n^s\ln n
    $$
    for some $\Tilde{C} = \Tilde{C}(r,s,\varepsilon)$.

    Finally, the last thing to notice is that $V_i \cup U_i$ contains $I$.

    Using these three properties we can see that the collection of all possible $V_i \cup U_i$ is indeed a container, each set $V_i \cup U_i$ is of size at most $(1 + \varepsilon/2 + o_n(1))\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1} \leq (1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}$ and there are at most 
    $$
        \sum_{j = 0}^{\left\lfloor\Tilde{C}n^s\ln n\right\rfloor} \binom{\binom{n}{r}}{j} = \exp\left(O(n^s\ln^2 n)\right)
    $$
    such sets, which is exactly what we need.

name: Proof of the lemma

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us consider an arbitrary independent set $I$ in $G(n,r,0)$ and perform the following algorithm. Put $V_0 = V_{G(n,r,0)}$ and $U_0 = \varnothing$. At $i$-th step select the vertex $v_i$ with maximum degree in $G(n,r,0)[V_{i-1}]$. If $v_i \in I$, put $V_i = V_{i-1} \setminus (\{v_i\} \cup N(v_i))$ and $U_i = U_{i-1} \cup \{v_i\}$. If $v_i \notin I$, we put $V_i = V_{i-1} \setminus \{v_i\}$ and $U_i = U_{i-1}$. We stop whenever $|V_i| \leq (1+\varepsilon/2)\binom{n-1}{r-1}$. In the remaining part of the proof index $i$ denotes the last step of the algorithm (that is, $|V_i| \leq (1+\varepsilon/2)\binom{n-1}{r-1}$).
	
	Let us obtain some properties of $V_i$ and $U_i$. First of all, let us notice that $V_i$ is a function of $U_i$. Indeed, if two independent sets $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the same on $V_{G(n,r,0)} \setminus V_i$, the algorithm does just the same steps for them and thus the final sets will be the same. This means that the number of different $V_i \cup U_i$ over all $I$ is exactly the same as the number of different $U_i$. 
	
	The second thing to notice is that whenever we add a vertex to $U_{j+1}$, we throw out $\Delta(G(n,r,0)[V_j])+1$ vertices from $V_j$. This can be trivially bounded from below with the use of Theorem \ref{Spectr}: 
	
	$$
		\Delta(G(n,r,0)[V_j]) \geq \frac{2e(G(n,r,0)[V_j])}{|V_j|} \geq \binom{n-r-1}{r-1}\frac{|V_j| - \binom{n-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n-1}{r-1}} \geq \frac{\varepsilon / 2}{1 + \varepsilon / 2}\frac{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n-1}{r-1}}|V_j|.
	$$
	
	We thus have 
	\begin{multline*}
		|V_{j+1}| \leq \left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2 + \varepsilon}\frac{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n-1}{r-1}}\right)|V_j| \Rightarrow \\ 
		\Rightarrow 1 \leq |V_{i-1}| \leq \left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2 + \varepsilon}\frac{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n-1}{r-1}}\right)^{|U_i|-1}\binom{n}{r} \leq \\ 
		\leq  \exp\left\{-\frac{\varepsilon}{2 + \varepsilon}\frac{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n-1}{r-1}}(|U_i|-1)\right\}\binom{n}{r} \Rightarrow \\
		\Rightarrow |U_i| \leq 1 + \frac{(2+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\varepsilon\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}} \leq \frac{2(2+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\varepsilon\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}.
	\end{multline*}
	    
	Note that since $n \geq 3r$, we have 
	$$
		\frac{2(2+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\varepsilon\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}} \leq  2\frac{3^{10} 9!\binom{n-1}{r-1}}{\varepsilon n^8} \leq 2\frac{3^{10}9!}{n^7}\binom{n-1}{r-1} \leq \frac{100}{n^2}\binom{n-1}{r-1} \leq \frac{1}{10n}\binom{n-1}{r-1}
	$$
	and thus $|U_i \cup V_i| \leq \left(1 + \varepsilon/2 + \frac{1}{10n}\right)\binom{n-1}{r-1} \leq (1+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}$.
	
	Finally, the last thing to notice is that $V_i \cup U_i$ contains $I$.

	Now we put all of this together to obtain that the set of all possible $U_i \cup V_i$ is indeed a container, each $V_i \cup U_i$ has size at most $(1+\varepsilon)\binom{n-1}{r-1}$ and the number of distinct $V_i \cup U_i$ is at most
	$$
		S = \sum_{i = 0}^{k}\binom{\binom{n}{r}}{i}.
	$$
	Since $k \leq \binom{n-1}{r-1} = \frac{r}{n}\binom{n}{r} \leq \frac{1}{3}\binom{n}{r}$, we have 
	$$
		\binom{\binom{n}{r}}{i} \binom{\binom{n}{r}}{i+1}^{-1} = \frac{(i+1)}{\binom{n}{r}-i} \leq \frac{1}{2}
	$$
	for $i < k$ and thus
	$$
		S \leq 2\binom{\binom{n}{r}}{k} \leq 2\left(\frac{\binom{n}{r}e}{k}\right)^{k}.
	$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and let us take $\delta = (1-\varepsilon)\frac{r-2s-1}{8\ln 2\binom{r}{s+1}}$. The main idea is the following. We take $2q = 2\left\lfloor\delta \binom{n}{s+1}\ln n\right\rfloor$ colors and randomly assign each vertex a list containing half of these colors. Assume that we managed to color our graph properly. Let $B_i$ be the set of vertices of color $i$. Then $B_i$ is contained in some set from (any) container. This means that we can assign each color $c$ a set $\varphi(c)$ from the container such that for each $i$ and each $v \in B_i$ we have at least one $C$ from the container such that $v \in C$ and $\varphi(i) = C$. It remains to prove that with positive probability for any $\varphi$ there exists at least one such $v$ that $v \notin \bigcup_{j = 1}^{q} \varphi(c_j)$, where $\{c_1, \dotsc, c_q\}$ is the list of colors assigned to $v$. We call $\varphi$ with this condition bad and all other $\varphi$ good.

    Let us now give a rigorous proof. Consider the $(2, \exp\{Cn^{s}\ln^2n\})$-container $\mathcal{C}$ from Lemma \ref{mainL}. Let us fix some function $\varphi$ that maps each color to some set $C \in \mathcal{C}$. Let us bound the probability that $\varphi$ is good. Let $\mathcal{C}(v)$ be the collection of all sets in $\mathcal{C}$ containing $v$. Let also $\mathrm{list}(v)$ be the list of colors for $v$. Finally, put $\xi_v = \mathbbm{1}\left\{\mathrm{list}(v) \cap \varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v)) = \varnothing\right\}$. Then $\varphi$ is good if and only if $\sum_{i =1}^{\binom{n}{r}}\xi_i = 0$. Since all $\xi_i$ are independent, we have
    $$
        \mathbf{P}\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{\binom{n}{r}}\xi_i = 0\right) = \prod_{i = 1}^{\binom{n}{r}}\mathbf{P}(\xi_i = 0).
    $$

    Let us now bound $\mathbf{P}(\xi_v = 0)$. In fact we will not bound all such probabilities, but only the ones with small $\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))$. Note that since each $C \in \mathcal{C}$ is of size at most $2\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}$, we have that 
    $$
    \sum_{v = 1}^{\binom{n}{r}}|\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))| = \sum_{c = 1}^{2q}|\varphi(c)| \leq 4q\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}.
    $$
    We thus obtain that there are at most $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}$ vertices such that 
    $$
    |\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))| \geq \frac{8q\binom{n-s-1}{r-s-1}}{\binom{n}{r}} \leq 8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln n.
    $$

    Now consider any $v$ such that $|\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))| \leq 8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln n$. We can bound $\mathbf{P}(\xi_v = 0)$ for big enough $n$ as follows.
    \begin{multline*}
        \mathbf{P}(\xi_v = 0) = 1- \mathbf{P}(\xi_v = 1) = 1 -\frac{\binom{2q-|\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))|}{q}}{\binom{2q}{q}} = 1 -\prod_{i = 0}^{q-1}\frac{2q-|\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))| - i}{2q-i} \leq \\ \leq 1 - \left(\frac{q -8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln n}{2q}\right)^{8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln n} \leq 1 - 2^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln n} = 1 - n^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln 2}. 
    \end{multline*}

    We thus have
    $$
         \mathbf{P}\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{\binom{n}{r}}\xi_i = 0\right) \leq \left(1 - n^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln 2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}} \leq \exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}n^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln 2}\right\}.
    $$
    It remains to notice that taking union bound over all $\varphi$ yields 
    \begin{multline*}
        \mathbf{P}(\text{exists at least } 1 \text{ good } \varphi) \leq (\exp\{Cn^s\ln^2 n\})^{2\delta n^{s+1}\ln n}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}n^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln 2}\right\} = \\ = \exp\left\{2\delta Cn^{2s+1}\ln^3 n - \frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}n^{-(1+\varepsilon)8\delta\binom{r}{s+1}\ln 2}\right\} = \\ = \exp\{2\delta Cn^{2s+1}\ln^3 n - \Omega(n^{r-(1-\varepsilon^2)(r-2s-1)})\} = o(1).
    \end{multline*}
    It remains to notice that we are done since $\varepsilon$ can be made arbitrarily small.

We take $2q = 2\left\lfloor\delta n \ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)\right\rfloor$ colors and randomly assign each vertex a list containing half of these colors.     		|\varphi^{-1}(\mathcal{C}(v))| \geq \frac{8q\binom{n-1}{r-1}}{\binom{n}{r}} \leq 8\delta r \ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right).
    	$$

    	\end{multline*}

	$$
         		\mathbf{P}\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{\binom{n}{r}}\xi_i = 0\right) \leq \left(1 - n^{-12\delta\frac{ r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}} \leq \exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right\}.

		\mathbf{P}(\text{exists at least } 1 \text{ good } \varphi) \leq 2^{2q}\left(\frac{e\binom{n}{r}}{k}\right)^{2kq}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right\} = \\ 
		= \exp\left(2q\ln 2 + 2kq + 2kq\ln\binom{n}{r} - 2kq\ln k - \frac12\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right) \leq \\
		\leq \exp\left(4kqr\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - 2kq\ln k - \frac12\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right) \leq \\ 
		\leq \exp\left(4kqr\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - \frac12\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right) \leq \\
		\leq  \exp\left(25\delta rn\frac{\binom{n-1}{r-1}\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)\ln \binom{n}{r}}{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - \frac12\binom{n}{r}n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right) \leq \\
		\leq  \exp\left(\binom{n}{r}\left(25\delta \frac{r^3}{\binom{n-r-1}{r-1}}\ln^3\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - \frac12n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right)\right) \leq \\
		\leq  \exp\left(\binom{n}{r}\left(25\delta \frac{r!r^2}{(n-2r)^{r-1}}\ln^3\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - \frac12n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right)\right) \leq \\ 
		\leq  \exp\left(\binom{n}{r}\left(\frac{r^{r+3}}{n^{r-1}}\ln^3\left(\frac{en}{r}\right) - \frac12n^{-12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}}\right)\right).
    \end{multline*}
   
	That is, if inequality 
	$$
		-r+1+(r+3)\frac{\ln r}{\ln n} \leq 4 - r\left(1-\frac{\ln r}{\ln n}\right) < -12\delta\frac{r\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n},
	$$
	holds we are done. A sufficient condition is
	$$
		r\left(1-\frac{\ln r}{\ln n}-12\delta\frac{\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)}{\ln n}\right) = r\left(1-12\delta-\frac{12\delta}{\ln n} - (1-12\delta)\frac{\ln r}{\ln n}\right) = (1-12\delta)r\left(1 - \frac{\ln r}{\ln n}\right) - \frac{12\delta r}{\ln n} > 4.
	$$
	Using the fact that $4\ln n \leq r \leq n/20$ and $\delta = \frac{1}{120}$, we can see that
	$$
 		 (1-12\delta)r\left(1 - \frac{\ln r}{\ln n}\right) - \frac{12\delta r}{\ln n} \geq 0.9r\frac{\ln 20}{\ln n} - \frac{0.1}{\ln n}r \geq \frac{\ln 20}{2\ln n}r \geq 2\ln 20 > 4
	$$ 
	and thus we are done.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathbf{Q}$ be the distribution on independent sets that minimizes $\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I)$. For each color $c$ let us assign it to a random set $I_c$ independently from everything else according to distribution $\mathbf{Q}$. Now for any vertex $v$ and color $c$ we say that $c$ is good for $v$ if $v \in I_c$ and $c$ is in $\mathrm{list}(v)$. Now we need to bound the probability that for each $v$ we have at least one good color. 
    
    Note that since $\mathbf{Q}$ is taken to minimize $\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I)$ and $I_c$ has distribution $\mathbf{Q}$ we have $$\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I_c) = \chi_f(G)$$ and thus
    $$
        \mathbf{Q}(v \in I_c) \geq \frac{1}{\chi_f(G)}
    $$
    for any $v \in G$ and any color $c \in \mathrm{list}(v)$. Now the probability that there is no good color for $v$ can be bounded from above as $(1 - \chi_f^{-1}(G))^{k} \leq \exp\{-k\chi_f^{-1}(G)\} \leq (en)^{-1}$ and it remains to apply the union bound over all $v \in G$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix some lists of size $k$ for all vertices.
    
    Take $l = \left\lceil\frac{\chi_f(G)}{\sqrt{\ln a(G)}}\right\rceil$ and $p = \frac{2l}{k}$. For each color in at least one of the lists we say that it is a reserve color with probability $p$ and main color otherwise. We do this independently for all colors. Let us now notice that for each vertex $v$ we have $\xi_v \sim Bin(k,p)$ reserve colors. 

    It is easy to prove that there exists a coloring such that $\xi_v \in [l, 3l]$ for all $v$ simultaneously. Indeed, we have $\mathbf{E} \xi_v = 2l$ and thus due to Chernoff's bound
    $$
       1-\mathbf{P}(\xi_v \in [l, 3l]) = \mathbf{P}\left(|\xi_v - \mathbf{E}\xi_v| > \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{E}\xi_v\right) \leq 2e^{-l/5} < 2n^{-2}.
    $$
    Taking union bound over all $v$ gives the desired result.

    So we split all the colors into main and reserve. For now, drop all reserve colors from the lists, so only main colors are left. Note that the size of each list is still at least 
    $$
        k - 3l = \lceil\chi_f(G)\left(\ln a(G) + \ln \ln a(G)\right)\rceil.
    $$

    Now let us perform the proof of Theorem \ref{UB1} with slight modifications. Let $\mathbf{Q}$ be the distribution on independent sets that minimizes $\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I)$. For each color $c$ let us assign it to a random set $I_c$ independently from everything else according to distribution $\mathbf{Q}$. Now for any vertex $v$ and color $c$ we say that $c$ is good for $v$ if $v \in I_c$ and $c$ is in $\mathrm{list}(v)$. The next thing to do is to bound the probability that for a vertex $v$ we have at least one good color $c$
    
    Note that since $\mathbf{Q}$ is taken to minimize $\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I)$ and $I_c$ has distribution $\mathbf{Q}$ we have $$\max_{v} \mathbf{Q}^{-1}(v \in I_c) = \chi_f(G)$$ and thus
    $$
        \mathbf{Q}(v \in I_c) \geq \frac{1}{\chi_f(G)}
    $$
    for any $v \in G$ and any color $c \in \mathrm{list}(v)$. Now the probability that there is no good color for $v$ can be bounded from above as 
    $$
    (1 - \chi_f^{-1}(G))^{k-3l} \leq \exp\{-(k-3l)\chi_f^{-1}(G)\} \leq \exp\{-\ln a(G) - \ln \ln a(G)\} \leq \frac{1}{a(G)\ln a(G)}.
    $$
    We can now obtain the bound on the expected number of vertices without good color. If $X$ is this number, then $\mathbf{E} X \leq \frac{n}{a(G)\ln a(G)}$. We can now use Markov inequality to obtain
    $$
        \mathbf{Q}(X > l) \leq \frac{\mathbf{E} X}{l} \leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln a(G)}} \leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln 3}} < 1.
    $$
    We can thus choose the sets $I_c$ in such a way that at most $l$ vertices will remain uncolored. But we can then easily color them using the reserve colors (since each list contains at least $l$ of those).
